question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Any declarations or practices of religious antipathy against ethnic minorities in a democratic country should not be tolerated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enmity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Antipathy" means a deep-seated feeling of dislike, hostility or aversion. Its closest synonym is "enmity" (the state of being an enemy; active hostility). (घृणा / शत्रुता)

◦ Example: There was a long-standing antipathy/enmity between the two communities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Passivity" (inactivity, acceptance without resistance), Option 2 "Devaluation" (reduction in value) and Option 4 "Conformity" (compliance with rules) do not carry the sense of dislike.

NOTE

• Synonyms of antipathy: enmity, hostility, aversion, animosity, hatred, repugnance. Antonyms: affinity, sympathy, fondness, rapport.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
option_2: The intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
option_3: An intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
option_4: The intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a singular countable noun is mentioned for the first time and is non-specific, we use the indefinite article "a/an". "explorer" and "cavern" are introduced for the first time, so they take "an intrepid explorer" and "an uncharted cavern".

• The phrase "the heart of the rainforest" is a specific/unique location, so it correctly takes the definite article "the".

◦ Correct: An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 wrongly use "the" for the first-mention nouns or "a heart" instead of the fixed phrase "the heart of the rainforest".

NOTE

• Use "a/an" for a non-specific singular noun mentioned for the first time; use "the" for something specific, already known, or unique (the heart, the sun, the moon).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Everyone disliked the new CEO, Kushal, but nobody is ready to put themselves in dangerous situation by telling him their feelings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bell the cat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to bell the cat" means to take on a dangerous or risky task on behalf of others; to dare to do something difficult. It fits "put themselves in a dangerous situation by telling him their feelings". (जोखिम भरा काम करने का बीड़ा उठाना)

◦ Example: Everyone wanted the rule changed, but no one was willing to bell the cat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sit on the fence" (to remain neutral/undecided), Option 2 "rule the roost" (to be in charge/dominate) and Option 3 "pull a long face" (to look sad/sulky) do not fit.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from the fable in which mice plan to hang a bell on the cat, but none dares to actually do it — hence "to bell the cat".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Even if an unlaced shoe is spotless, it is not neat.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. soiled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Spotless" means perfectly clean; without any stain or mark. Its antonym is "soiled", meaning dirty or stained. (बेदाग़ का विलोम — गंदा / मैला)

◦ Example: She kept the kitchen spotless, but the children's clothes were soiled with mud.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "agile" (quick-moving), Option 3 "forged" (fake/counterfeit) and Option 4 "requisite" (necessary) are unrelated to cleanliness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of spotless: immaculate, unblemished, pristine, clean. Antonyms: soiled, dirty, stained, filthy, grubby.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He pressed the _________ just in time to avoid the accident.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. brake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brake" (a noun) is the device used to slow down or stop a vehicle. To avoid an accident, one presses the brake. (ब्रेक)

◦ Correct: He pressed the brake just in time to avoid the accident.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "break" is a homophone meaning to separate into pieces or a pause/rest — not a vehicle part.

• Option 2 "bike" and Option 4 "beak" (a bird's mouth) do not fit the context.

NOTE

• Homophones: brake (stop a vehicle) vs break (to shatter / an interval). "Apply the brakes" but "take a break".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Raju is lazy and smart, but he does not attend the classes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. industrious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lazy" means unwilling to work or make an effort; idle. Its antonym is "industrious", meaning hardworking and diligent. (आलसी का विलोम — परिश्रमी)

◦ Example: Unlike his lazy brother, Raju was industrious and hardworking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "snobbish" (arrogant), Option 2 "lax" (careless/not strict — actually a near-synonym of lazy) and Option 4 "genius" (highly talented) are not correct antonyms of "lazy".

NOTE

• Synonyms of industrious: diligent, hardworking, assiduous, conscientious. Antonyms: lazy, idle, indolent, slothful.

question:
Correct the underlined part of the sentence.

This mango is bitterer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bitter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence has no second object of comparison (no "than ..."), so the comparative degree "bitterer" is wrong. The simple positive degree "bitter" should be used. (तुलना न होने पर मूल रूप)

◦ Correct: This mango is bitter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "more bitter" (Option 2) and "bitterest"/"most bitter" (Options 1, 3) are comparative/superlative forms, which need a comparison or a group — absent here.

• Note: the standard comparative of "bitter" is "more bitter", not "bitterer".

NOTE

• Degree of comparison: use the positive when no comparison is made (This mango is bitter), the comparative with "than" (more bitter than that one), and the superlative with "the" for a group (the most bitter of all).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Occurrance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Occurrance" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Occurrence", meaning an event or incident. (घटना)

◦ Spelling key: OC + CUR + RENCE (double "c", double "r", ends in "-ence").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Conscious" (aware), "Receive" (to get — remember "i before e except after c") and "Believe" (to accept as true) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words often misspelt: occurrence, recommend, accommodate, embarrass, privilege. "Occur" doubles the final "r" before "-ence/-ing/-ed" (occurred, occurring, occurrence).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Depresed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Depresed" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Depressed", meaning very unhappy/low in spirits. (उदास / अवसादग्रस्त)

◦ Spelling key: DE + PRESS + ED (double "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Battle" (a fight), "Comfortable" (giving comfort) and "Cheerful" (happy) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The verb "press" keeps its double "s" in derivatives: depress → depressed, depression; impress → impressed, impression.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

My brother asked me, "Can I exchange my phone from you?"
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. my phone with yours.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "exchange" takes the preposition "with" — we exchange one thing with another. So the correct phrase is "exchange my phone with yours". (के साथ अदला-बदली करना)

◦ Correct: Can I exchange my phone with yours?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "exchange ... from/since/within yours" (Options 2, 3, 4) use wrong prepositions.

• The possessive pronoun "yours" correctly avoids repeating "your phone".

NOTE

• Collocation: "exchange A for B" (goods for money) and "exchange A with someone" (swap). Here we swap phones, so "with yours" is right.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Inflamous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inflamous" is misspelt. The correct word is "Infamous", meaning well known for a bad quality or deed; notorious. (कुख्यात)

◦ Spelling key: IN + FA + MOUS (no "l").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Arrangement" (an orderly plan), "Kerbstone" (British spelling of the stone edging a pavement) and "Subjugator" (one who subdues/conquers) are correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Note the pair famous (well known for good) vs infamous (well known for bad). The related noun is "infamy".

question:
Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'.

(A) She sings / (B) the song / (C) beautiful in the party / (D) No error.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Segment (C) "beautiful in the party" contains the error. "beautiful" is an adjective, but here we need an adverb to modify the verb "sings". The correct word is "beautifully".

◦ Correct: She sings the song beautifully in the party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segments (A) "She sings" and (B) "the song" are grammatically correct.

• Adverbs of manner (often ending in "-ly") describe how an action is done: sings beautifully, runs quickly, writes neatly.

NOTE

• Adjectives modify nouns (a beautiful song); adverbs modify verbs/adjectives/adverbs (sings beautifully). Do not use an adjective where an adverb is needed.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Most women are facing the same problem when it comes to job satisfaction because of the pay parity in institutions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in the same boat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in the same boat" means in the same difficult or unfortunate situation as others. It fits "facing the same problem". (एक ही मुसीबत में होना)

◦ Example: With prices rising, we are all in the same boat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "armchair experts" (people who give opinions without real experience), Option 2 "a drop in the ocean" (a very small, insignificant amount) and Option 3 "comparing apples to oranges" (comparing two very different things) do not fit.

NOTE

• "In the same boat" emphasises shared hardship. Similar: "in the same predicament", "sailing in the same boat".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The ancient Greeks and pagans used to worship natural _________ as Gods and Goddesses.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. elements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Elements" here means the natural forces/components of nature (such as the sun, wind, fire, water, earth), which ancient peoples worshipped as deities. (प्राकृतिक तत्व)

◦ Correct: The ancient Greeks and pagans used to worship natural elements as Gods and Goddesses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "impulses" (sudden urges), Option 2 "mixtures" (combinations of substances) and Option 3 "instincts" (innate tendencies) cannot be "worshipped as Gods".

NOTE

• The classical "four elements" were earth, water, air and fire — often personified as gods in ancient mythologies.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: The traffic on a highway was heavy during an evening.
option_2: The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.
option_3: The traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
option_4: A traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Traffic" is an uncountable noun, so it does not take "a" (Option 4 "A traffic" is wrong).

• "highway" and "evening" here refer to specific ones, so they take the definite article "the" — "on the highway", "during the evening".

◦ Correct: The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 3 wrongly use "a highway" or "an evening" for a specific, understood reference.

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns (traffic, water, information, advice, furniture) do not take "a/an" and have no plural form: "heavy traffic", not "a traffic/traffics".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am calling to thank you _________ the present you sent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "thank" is followed by the preposition "for" when we mention the reason. We thank someone for something. (के लिए धन्यवाद देना)

◦ Correct: I am calling to thank you for the present you sent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "thank you with/of/in" (Options 2, 3, 4) are all incorrect collocations.

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: "thank someone for something" (Thank you for your help). Similarly: apologise for, apologise to someone, congratulate someone on something.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future perfect tense form.

I hope you wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.
option_1: I hope you will have washed all the clothes before you come into the house again.
option_2: I hope you shall wash all the clothes before you come into the house again
option_3: I hope you will be washing all the clothes before you come into the house again.
option_4: I hope you will have wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I hope you will have washed all the clothes before you come into the house again.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The future perfect tense is formed as "will have + past participle (V3)". The past participle of "wash" is "washed". So "will have washed". (भविष्य पूर्ण काल)

◦ Correct: I hope you will have washed all the clothes before you come into the house again.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "shall wash" is simple future; Option 3 "will be washing" is future continuous.

• Option 4 "will have wash" is wrong — it uses the base form "wash" instead of the past participle "washed".

NOTE

• Future perfect describes an action that will be completed before a certain future time, e.g., by 5 p.m. I will have finished the report.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Rose painted the most beautifullest picture ever at the art class today!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the most beautifullest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "the most beautifullest" is a double superlative and is grammatically wrong. The superlative of "beautiful" is either "the most beautiful" (correct) — never "most beautifullest".

◦ Correct: Rose painted the most beautiful picture ever at the art class today!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Rose painted", "picture ever at the" and "art class today!" are correct.

• "beautifullest" is itself an incorrect form; combining it with "most" makes it doubly wrong.

NOTE

• Never combine "most" with the "-est" ending, or "more" with "-er". Say "the most beautiful", "the tallest" — not "most tallest" or "more taller".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

one who does something for pleasure
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Hedonist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "hedonist" is a person who believes that pleasure is the most important thing in life and does things for pleasure. (सुखवादी / भोगवादी)

◦ Example: A hedonist lives to enjoy food, comfort and entertainment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anarchist" (one who opposes all government), Option 2 "Atheist" (one who does not believe in God) and Option 4 "Aggressor" (one who attacks first) do not fit.

NOTE

• Related terms: hedonism (the pursuit of pleasure), epicurean (fond of luxury/good food). Contrast with ascetic (one who avoids pleasures).

question:
Select the most appropriate word to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Rohit asked Nita what was the most intriguing book she has read recently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. tedious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word that substitutes the underlined word in the sentence is "tedious", meaning too long, slow and boring; monotonous. (उबाऊ / थकाऊ)

◦ Example: The lecture was so tedious that many students fell asleep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "arraigned" (formally charged/accused in court), Option 3 "encircled" (surrounded) and Option 4 "subdued" (quietened/brought under control) do not fit the context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tedious: boring, dull, monotonous, wearisome, humdrum. Antonyms: interesting, exciting, engaging, absorbing.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Newspapers are like mirrors (1)___________ the diverse facets of society, capturing the voices, stories, and events that define our shared human experience. They serve as a forum (2)___________ dialogue, debate, and discussion, amplifying voices from all walks of life and fostering (3)___________ sense of community. Beyond reporting news, newspapers also celebrate achievements, highlight cultural (4)___________, and showcase human resilience in the face of adversity. They are archives of history, chronicling the triumphs and trials of generations, and serving as a reminder of how far we have come and how much further we can go. In an age of digital transformation, newspapers continue to (5)___________, adapting to new mediums while upholding the core values of journalism: accuracy, integrity, and accountability.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reflecting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a present participle (V-ing) acting as a modifier that describes what the "mirrors" do. "mirrors reflecting the diverse facets of society" correctly uses the participle to add descriptive information.

◦ Correct: Newspapers are like mirrors reflecting the diverse facets of society ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "reflect" (base form) and 2 "reflects" (finite verb) would make the clause grammatically incomplete after "mirrors".

• Option 4 "reflected" (past participle) would give a passive sense, which does not suit here.

NOTE

• A present participle phrase ("reflecting ...") often follows a noun to describe it, equivalent to "which reflect ...": mirrors reflecting = mirrors which reflect.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

◦ Correct: They serve as a forum for dialogue, debate, and discussion ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

question:

Newspapers are like mirrors (1)___________ the diverse facets of society, capturing the voices, stories, and events that define our shared human experience. They serve as a forum (2)___________ dialogue, debate, and discussion, amplifying voices from all walks of life and fostering (3)___________ sense of community. Beyond reporting news, newspapers also celebrate achievements, highlight cultural (4)___________, and showcase human resilience in the face of adversity. They are archives of history, chronicling the triumphs and trials of generations, and serving as a reminder of how far we have come and how much further we can go. In an age of digital transformation, newspapers continue to (5)___________, adapting to new mediums while upholding the core values of journalism: accuracy, integrity, and accountability.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "sense" is a singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound, and here it is non-specific, so it takes the indefinite article "a" — "fostering a sense of community". (अनिश्चित उपपद 'a')

◦ Correct: ... amplifying voices from all walks of life and fostering a sense of community.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "an" (Option 3) is used before a vowel sound, but "sense" begins with the consonant /s/.

• "the" (Option 2) would wrongly make it specific; "No article" (Option 1) is wrong because a singular countable noun needs a determiner.

NOTE

• "a sense of ..." is a common fixed phrase: a sense of community, a sense of belonging, a sense of humour.

question:

Newspapers are like mirrors (1)___________ the diverse facets of society, capturing the voices, stories, and events that define our shared human experience. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. richness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the adjective "cultural", a noun is needed as the object of "highlight". "richness" is the noun form (meaning abundance/wealth of something). "highlight cultural richness" is correct. (सांस्कृतिक समृद्धि)

◦ Correct: ... newspapers also celebrate achievements, highlight cultural richness ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "richest" (superlative adjective) and Option 2 "richer" (comparative adjective) cannot serve as the object noun here.

• Option 4 "richly" is an adverb, which also cannot be the object of "highlight".

NOTE

• Word forms of "rich": rich (adjective), richness (noun), richly (adverb), enrich (verb). Here a noun is required.

question:

Newspapers are like mirrors (1)___________ the diverse facets of society, capturing the voices, stories, and events that define our shared human experience. They serve as a forum (2)___________ dialogue, debate, and discussion, amplifying voices from all walks of life and fostering (3)___________ sense of community. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. evolve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Evolve" means to develop gradually; to change and adapt over time. In "an age of digital transformation, newspapers continue to evolve, adapting to new mediums", it fits perfectly. (विकसित होना)

◦ Correct: ... newspapers continue to evolve, adapting to new mediums ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dissolve" (to break up/disappear), Option 2 "involve" (to include) and Option 4 "revolve" (to move in a circle) do not fit the idea of gradual development.

NOTE

• "Evolve" pairs naturally with "adapt": adapting to new mediums = evolving. Synonyms: develop, progress, advance, grow, transform.

question: The Iron Age site named Tekwada is located in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Iron Age archaeological site of Tekwada is located in Maharashtra. It is associated with early iron-using (megalithic) cultures of the region. (तेकवाड़ा — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Iron Age in India (roughly from about 1200–1000 BCE) saw the spread of iron tools and is linked with the Painted Grey Ware (PGW) and megalithic cultures.

• Maharashtra has several important megalithic and early historic sites.

NOTE

• Other early iron sites in India include Malhar, Dadupur (UP) and Hallur (Karnataka), which show early evidence of iron working.

question: Rabindranath Tagore referred to ____________ as Nritya Samragini, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitara Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rabindranath Tagore referred to Sitara Devi as "Nritya Samragini" (the empress of dance) after being impressed by her performance. She was a legendary Kathak dancer. (सितारा देवी — नृत्य साम्राज्ञी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sitara Devi (1920–2014) was born in Kolkata to a Kathak family; she received the Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms, originating in North India.

NOTE

• Mrinalini Sarabhai and Rukmini Devi Arundale were famous Bharatanatyam exponents; Rukmini Devi founded Kalakshetra in Chennai.

question: The term 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are associated with which crop in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paddy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aus", "Aman" and "Boro" are the three main cropping seasons/varieties of rice (paddy), especially in West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh. (धान की तीन फसलें)

◦ Aus (autumn/pre-monsoon), Aman (winter/main kharif crop) and Boro (summer, irrigated).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rice is a kharif crop requiring high temperature (above 25°C) and high humidity/rainfall (above 100 cm).

• India is one of the largest producers of rice; West Bengal is the leading rice-producing state.

NOTE

• Cropping seasons in India: Kharif (sown June–July, e.g., rice, maize, cotton), Rabi (sown Oct–Dec, e.g., wheat, gram) and Zaid (summer, e.g., watermelon, cucumber).

question: How many chances does a high jumper get for overcoming a certain height?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three chances.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the athletics event of the high jump, a jumper gets three chances (attempts) to clear a particular height. Three consecutive failures (at any height) eliminate the athlete. (हाई जंप — तीन प्रयास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The high jump is a track-and-field event where athletes jump over a horizontal bar; the popular technique is the "Fosbury Flop".

• The same "three attempts" rule applies to events like the long jump, pole vault (per height) and shot put/discus/javelin (in the final rounds).

NOTE

• Athletics is governed internationally by World Athletics (formerly IAAF). The men's high jump world record (2.45 m) is held by Javier Sotomayor of Cuba.

question: Which of the following is the correct statement about the Rajya Sabha?
option_1: All the members are directly elected by the people.
option_2: It is known as the Council of the States.
option_3: It is known as the lower house of the parliament.
option_4: The term of the members is for 5 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is known as the Council of the States.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament and is known as the "Council of States". Its members are indirectly elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies. (राज्य सभा — राज्यों की परिषद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house (it is never fully dissolved); one-third of its members retire every two years, so each member's term is 6 years (not 5).

• The Lok Sabha is the lower house (House of the People), directly elected for a 5-year term.

• Maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated by the President).

NOTE

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha.

question: Which Census decade recorded the highest population growth rate (in terms of percentage) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961-1971.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census decade 1961–1971 recorded the highest decadal population growth rate (about 24.8%) in India's census history. (सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर — 1961-71)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The year 1921 is called the "Great Divide/Demographic Divide" — after it, India's population began growing rapidly and continuously.

• The 2001–2011 decade showed a growth rate of about 17.7%, lower than earlier decades, indicating a slowing of growth.

NOTE

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872 (under Lord Mayo) and the first complete/synchronous census in 1881 (under Lord Ripon). The census is conducted every 10 years.

question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is William Jones.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Asiatic Society of Bengal" was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784 at Calcutta (Kolkata) to promote the study of Indian history, languages, literature and culture. (एशियाटिक सोसाइटी ऑफ बंगाल — विलियम जोन्स, 1784)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sir William Jones was a British judge and Orientalist who noted the similarity between Sanskrit, Greek and Latin, laying the basis for the study of the Indo-European language family.

• The Society did pioneering work in deciphering ancient inscriptions and reviving interest in India's past.

NOTE

• Warren Hastings (Governor-General) was a patron of Orientalist studies and set up the Calcutta Madrasa (1781). James Prinsep, who deciphered the Brahmi script, was also associated with the Society.

question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights entails trafficking of human beings and forced labour?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rights against Exploitation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Right against Exploitation" (Articles 23 and 24) prohibits trafficking of human beings, begar (forced labour) and the employment of children below 14 years in hazardous work. (शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 23-24)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 23 — prohibits human trafficking and forced labour.

• Article 24 — prohibits child labour in factories, mines and hazardous employment.

• The six Fundamental Rights are: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30) and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

NOTE

• Fundamental Rights are given in Part III (Articles 12–35) of the Constitution and are largely inspired by the US Bill of Rights.

question: The weaker warm storms that grow stronger over time are finally converted into huge storms or hurricanes. Which of the following climate regions is the origin of such hurricanes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical climate region.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hurricanes (tropical cyclones) originate over the warm ocean waters of the tropical climate region, where the sea-surface temperature is high (above about 27°C), providing the heat and moisture needed for the storm to grow. (उष्णकटिबंधीय जलवायु क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• These storms are called hurricanes in the Atlantic/eastern Pacific, typhoons in the western Pacific, and cyclones in the Indian Ocean.

• The calm centre of a hurricane is called the "eye".

NOTE

• Tropical cyclones need warm seas, high humidity and the Coriolis force to form; they do not form right at the equator (where the Coriolis force is zero).

question: The author of the Hindi novel 'Kohre Mein Kaid Rang' is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Govind Mishra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Kohre Mein Kaid Rang" was written by Govind Mishra, a distinguished Hindi novelist and short-story writer. (कोहरे में कैद रंग — गोविंद मिश्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Govind Mishra won the Sahitya Akademi Award (2008) for this novel and later received the Vyas Samman and Saraswati Samman.

• He is known for novels dealing with human relationships and the middle-class experience.

NOTE

• Kamleshwar (Kitne Pakistan), Uday Prakash (Peeli Chhatri Wali Ladki) and Chitra Mudgal (Aavan) are other noted Hindi writers.

question: In which of the following states is the Bissu Mela organised to thank Santoora Devi for the good harvest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bissu Mela" is a traditional fair organised in Uttarakhand (in the Jaunsar-Bawar region) to thank the goddess Santoora Devi for a good harvest and to celebrate the spring/new agricultural season. (बिस्सू मेला — उत्तराखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The fair features folk songs, dances (like the Thoda dance) and community feasting.

• Uttarakhand is known as "Dev Bhoomi" (Land of the Gods) and has many pilgrimage and cultural fairs.

NOTE

• Famous fairs of Uttarakhand include the Kumbh Mela (Haridwar), Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra and Uttarayani Mela (Bageshwar).

question: In june 2022, Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of Maharashtra in June 2022, after a split in the Shiv Sena, with the support of the BJP (Devendra Fadnavis became Deputy CM). (एकनाथ शिंदे — महाराष्ट्र के मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Maharashtra is India's second-most populous state; its capital is Mumbai (the financial capital of India) and winter capital is Nagpur.

• The Governor administers the oath of office to the Chief Minister (Article 164).

NOTE

• The Chief Minister is the real executive head of a state, while the Governor is the constitutional/nominal head.

question: Who among the following founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jyotiba Phule.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Satyashodhak Samaj" (Society of Truth-Seekers) was founded by Jyotiba Phule (Jyotirao Phule) in 1873 at Pune (Maharashtra) to fight caste discrimination and untouchability and to uplift the lower castes and women. (सत्यशोधक समाज — ज्योतिबा फुले, 1873)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jyotiba Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule were pioneers of women's education and started one of the first schools for girls in India.

• Phule wrote "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), attacking the caste system, and coined the term "Dalit".

NOTE

• Phule was given the title "Mahatma". He worked for the education and rights of Shudras, Ati-Shudras (untouchables) and women.

question: Which type of loan is supported by MUDRA?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Non-farm loan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) supports non-farm (non-agricultural) micro and small enterprises by providing loans up to ₹10 lakh (now enhanced) for small businesses. (मुद्रा — गैर-कृषि ऋण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched in 2015. Loans are given in three categories:

◦ Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000–₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5 lakh–₹10 lakh).

• These loans are collateral-free and aim to "fund the unfunded" small entrepreneurs.

NOTE

• MUDRA supports non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises such as shopkeepers, artisans, vendors and small manufacturers.

question: What is the percentage of 's' character in the carbon atom of acetylene?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In acetylene (C₂H₂, ethyne), each carbon atom is sp hybridised (it forms a triple bond). An sp hybrid orbital has one s and one p orbital, so the s-character is 1/2 = 50%. (एसीटिलीन — sp संकरण — 50% s-अक्षर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• s-character in common hybridisations:

◦ sp → 50% (e.g., acetylene/ethyne, triple bond),

◦ sp² → 33.33% (e.g., ethene, double bond),

◦ sp³ → 25% (e.g., methane/ethane, single bonds).

NOTE

• More s-character means the orbital is closer to the nucleus, so bonds are shorter and stronger, and the atom is more electronegative (this explains the acidity of terminal alkynes).

question: In Union Budget 2023, a sub-scheme of which of the following Yojanas has been proposed with the investment of ₹6,000 crore to enable activities of fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Matsya Sampada Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, a new sub-scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was announced with an investment of ₹6,000 crore to support fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises in the fisheries sector. (पीएम मत्स्य संपदा योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PMMSY was launched in 2020 to bring about a "Blue Revolution" through sustainable development of the fisheries sector.

• The sub-scheme (PM-MKSSY) aims to improve value chains, formalise the sector and expand markets.

NOTE

• India is one of the largest fish producers in the world. The fisheries sector comes under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

question: India launched the 'National Social Assistance Programme' in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)" was launched on 15 August 1995. It provides social assistance (pensions and benefits) to the poor, elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. (राष्ट्रीय सामाजिक सहायता कार्यक्रम — 1995)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• NSAP is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development and gives effect to the Directive Principles (Article 41 — right to assistance in old age, sickness and disablement).

• Its components include the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, Widow Pension Scheme, Disability Pension Scheme and the National Family Benefit Scheme.

NOTE

• NSAP targets Below Poverty Line (BPL) households, providing a basic level of financial support to the most vulnerable sections of society.

question: Which of the following Mughal emperors issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jahangir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mughal emperor Jahangir issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa (Nur Jahan), who wielded great influence in his court. (जहांगीर — नूरजहाँ के सम्मान में सिक्के)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nur Jahan ("Light of the World") was the powerful queen of Jahangir; coins were struck in her name and royal orders (farmans) were issued under her seal.

• Jahangir (r. 1605–1627) was the son of Akbar and was known for his interest in painting and justice (the "Chain of Justice").

NOTE

• The Mughal succession: Babur → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb. Shah Jahan (Jahangir's son) built the Taj Mahal for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

question: To which of the following groups do whales belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mammalia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Whales belong to the class Mammalia (mammals), not fish. They are warm-blooded, breathe air through lungs, give birth to live young and feed them with milk. (व्हेल — स्तनधारी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Whales, dolphins and porpoises are aquatic mammals belonging to the order Cetacea.

• The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth.

NOTE

• Key mammalian features: hair/fur, mammary glands (milk), a diaphragm for breathing, four-chambered heart and (usually) live birth. Other mammals include bats (fly) and humans.

question: Buddhadev Dasgupta was a famous instrumentalist of which of the following instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Buddhadev Dasgupta was a renowned Indian classical musician famous for playing the "Sarod". He belonged to the Senia Shahjahanpur gharana. (बुद्धदेव दासगुप्ता — सरोद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, known for its deep, resonant sound.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Other famous Sarod maestros include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Amjad Ali Khan. The Santoor is associated with Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and the Sitar with Pandit Ravi Shankar.

question: Who among the following received the Padma Shri 2021 for Panthi folk dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radhe Shyam Barle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Radhe Shyam Barle received the Padma Shri in 2021 for his contribution to the "Panthi" folk dance of Chhattisgarh. (राधे श्याम बारले — पंथी नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Panthi dance is performed by the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh, usually on Maghi Purnima to honour Guru Ghasidas.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India (after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan).

NOTE

• Bhuri Bai (a Bhil/Pithora artist of Madhya Pradesh) also received the Padma Shri for painting. Folk dances are often recognised through the Padma awards.

question:
Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by _________.
a) an abnormally heavy body weight
b) an intense fear of losing weight
c) a distorted perception of weight
d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
solution_text:
The correct answer is c and d.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anorexia Nervosa is a serious eating disorder characterised by:

◦ (c) a distorted perception of one's weight/body image (seeing oneself as overweight even when underweight), and

◦ (d) attempts to lose weight through excessive exercising, extreme dieting and self-starvation.

• It typically involves an abnormally LOW body weight and an intense fear of GAINING weight — so statements (a) "abnormally heavy body weight" and (b) "fear of losing weight" are the opposite of the truth. (एनोरेक्सिया नर्वोसा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• People with anorexia severely restrict food intake, leading to malnutrition and health complications.

• A related eating disorder is Bulimia Nervosa, marked by cycles of binge-eating followed by purging (vomiting).

NOTE

• Eating disorders are psychological/mental-health conditions and require both medical and psychological treatment.

question: Which of the following is NOT a physiographic division of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Tibetan Plateau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Tibetan Plateau" is NOT a physiographic division of India — it lies mainly in China (Tibet), to the north of the Himalayas. (तिब्बती पठार — भारत का भाग नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The six major physiographic divisions of India are:

◦ The Himalayan Mountains, The Northern Plains, The Peninsular Plateau, The Indian Desert (Thar), The Coastal Plains and The Islands.

NOTE

• The Peninsular Plateau is the oldest landmass of India; the Northern Plains are formed by the alluvium of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

question: Ujjwala was the mascot of which national sports event held in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khelo India Para Games 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ujjwala" was the official mascot of the first Khelo India Para Games 2023, held in New Delhi. (उज्ज्वला — खेलो इंडिया पैरा गेम्स 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Khelo India scheme was launched by the Government of India (2018) to revive the sports culture at the grassroots level.

• It includes the Khelo India Youth Games, University Games, Winter Games and the Para Games.

NOTE

• Mascots are used to promote sporting events; they usually reflect the culture or spirit of the host place. The Khelo India programme comes under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

question: In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the __________ directions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cardinal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Harappan (Indus Valley) civilisation, cities were carefully planned on a grid pattern, with streets and lanes generally oriented along the cardinal directions — North, South, East and West. (मुख्य दिशाओं — कार्डिनल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Harappan town planning featured a grid layout, an advanced covered drainage system, and buildings of standardised baked bricks.

• Cities were usually divided into a raised "Citadel" (west) and a "Lower Town" (east).

NOTE

• The four cardinal directions are N, S, E, W; the ordinal (intercardinal) directions are NE, NW, SE, SW. Major Harappan sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan and Rakhigarhi.
